text:
ConocoPhillips fell 4% today as crude oil prices dropped more than 7% on news of potential U.S.-Iran peace negotiations. When oil prices fall, energy companies' revenues and profits decline—the company's core business depends on selling oil at higher prices. The timing matters: diplomatic progress reduces the geopolitical risk premium that has been supporting oil prices, so traders sold oil futures aggressively, which immediately pressured the stock.

This move reverses the strong gain the stock posted just two trading days earlier (when it hit $154), which had likely been driven by escalating tensions and military posturing between the U.S. and Iran. Oil prices remain well above historical averages at $103 per barrel domestically and $123 globally, so the company still operates in a relatively supportive environment—but any shift toward de-escalation works against it in the short term.
